newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai bourse to widen trading price limit to 30 pct.
newsitem.headline: Thai bourse to widen trading price limit to 30 pct.

text.p: The Stock Exchange of Thailand will widen its daily floor/ceiling trading limit to 30 percent from an existing 10 percent next week, brokers said on Friday.

"The SET and all member brokers agreed to widen the (floor/ceiling) trading limit to 30 percent. However the SET board has yet to give final approval (on the widening)," Korn Chatikavanich, president of JF Thanakom Securities told reporters after meeting with the stock exchange officials on Friday afternoon.
The exchange currently allows shares to trade in a 10 percent range above or below the previous day's closing price.
A senior official at the SET confirmed the report and said the board was holding a meeting to discuss the matter and to set an implementation date.
"It seems like the daily trading limit will be 30 percent up and down from the previous day's close from next week," said a senior official at the SET.
"We are not sure which day yet but you can expect a press release wthin the next few hours," he said.
During the bourse's rally over the past three days, most major stocks jumped to their 10 percent upper daily limit within the first few hours of trade, and orders could not be completed.
"Once (the limit's raised) we'll see what this rally is all about," said one analyst.
Thai stocks have gained more than 130 points in the past three days. The key SET index was up 42.07 or 6.81 percent at 660.05 in late afternoon dealings.
